notes: Configuration snapshot effective 2026-08-24; volatile program parameters, never hardcoded truths. Additional sources: https://docs.polymarket.com/programs/maker-rebates, https://docs.polymarket.com/programs/taker-rebates, https://docs.polymarket.com/programs/liquidity-rewards, https://docs.polymarket.com/market-data/market-details. market_settings_example models the SDK-PARSED market.rewards layer (what a @polymarket/client consumer sees), NOT the raw Gamma HTTP body; re-verified 2026-08-26. The market-details page publishes both layers and they differ: its TypeScript tab types rewardsMinSize as DecimalString | null and rewardsAmount/rewardsDailyRate as DecimalString and prints them QUOTED ("rewardsMinSize": "100", "rewardsAmount": "10000", "rewardsDailyRate": "100"); its Python tab types them Decimal; its API (Gamma) tab types the same fields as number and prints them UNQUOTED. These agree once the SDK is taken into account: ClobRewardsSchema uses DecimalishSchema = z.union([DecimalStringSchema, z.number().transform(...)]), which accepts a JSON number on input and always outputs a decimal string (https://github.com/Polymarket/ts-sdk/blob/7fdbed42484b5d279c71aa36d3757d18968260da/packages/bindings/src/gamma/common.ts and .../shared.ts, retrieved 2026-08-26). rewardsMaxSpread stays a JSON number: it is number/float in every published representation. endDate is IsoCalendarDateString | null (Python date | None) -- null when the reward program has no end date -- so the second clobRewards entry freezes the null form. assetAddress is documented and implemented as a plain string (z.string()), not an EVM address. holdingRewardsEnabled completes the published MarketRewards field list (clobRewards, rewardsMinSize, rewardsMaxSpread, holdingRewardsEnabled) and is typed holdingRewardsEnabled?: boolean | null (Python holding_rewards_enabled: bool | None; Gamma field table 'boolean -- Indicates if holding rewards are active'; SDK z.boolean().nullish() in gamma/market.ts), so it is both optional and nullable; re-fetched read-only 2026-08-26. ITS VALUE HERE IS ILLUSTRATIVE: the page's Gamma JSON example omits the key entirely, so the frozen `true` demonstrates the documented boolean shape and asserts nothing about any real market's holding-reward status. All rates and shares are recorded as CANONICAL decimal strings per handoff SS7.3 (no trailing fractional zeros): the documented 20% pool share is recorded as "0.2", 50% as "0.5", the 1.0x-2.3x weight range as "1"-"2.3", the scaling factor 3.0 as "3", and the 0.10/0.90 single-sided band as "0.1"/"0.9". Canonicalization changes representation only, never the documented value; for the reward decimals the doc's own lexemes ("100", "10000") are already canonical, so no rewriting was applied to the first clobRewards entry. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE LIMIT: because these decimal strings are canonicalized (normalized) data, they CANNOT be used as evidence of the raw lexemes the venue puts on the wire -- for example whether the API serializes "0.20" or "0.2", or a JSON number rather than a string. Any future raw-wire capture must retain the venue's original strings verbatim in a separate fixture before wire-lexeme claims are made.
